text:
Predicates:
DeadlyDisease(x) ::: x is a deadly disease.
SurvivalRateLow(x) ::: x has a low survival rate.
SevereCancer(x) ::: x is a severe cancer.
BileDuctCancer(x) ::: x is a bile duct cancer.
Cholangiocarcinoma(x) ::: x is Cholangiocarcinoma.
MildFlu(x) ::: x is mild flu.
ColorectalCancer(x) ::: x is colorectal cancer.
SurvivalRateLow(x) ::: x has a low survival rate.
Premises:
∀x (DeadlyDisease(x) → SurvivalRateLow(x)) ::: If something is a deadly disease, then its survival rate is low.
∀x (SevereCancer(x) → DeadlyDisease(x)) ::: All severe cancers are deadly diseases.
SevereCancer(bileDuctCancer) ::: Bile duct cancer is a severe cancer.
∀x (Cholangiocarcinoma(x) → bileDuctCancer(x)) ::: All Cholangiocarcinoma are bile duct cancer.
∀x (MildFlu(x) → ¬SurvivalRateLow(x)) ::: No one with mild flu has a low survival rate.
∀x (ColorectalCancer(x) ∧ bileDuctCancer(x) ∧ SurvivalRateLow(x) → ¬bileDuctCancer(x)) ::: If colorectal cancer is a bile duct cancer and the survival rate is low, then colorectal cancer is not a bile duct cancer.
Conclusion:
SevereCancer(ColorectalCancer) ::: Colorectal cancer is a severe cancer.
